summary: Marianne Pieper studied at the University of Hamburg and completed her habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg in 1996. She held positions at Hamburg (1990–1994, 1996–2015) and the University of Kassel (1994–1996).

Marianne Winder was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, University of Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove, later working at Nottingham, London, and the Wellcome Trust.

Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Director of the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania under Sengaku Mayeda.
Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Dagpo Rinpoche and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Marina Illich is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 2006 under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths, later holding posts at Hampshire College (~2000–2006) and Rollins College (~2006).

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at UCLA under Robert Buswell in 2000, he taught at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz studied at the University of Bologna (~1914–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He held posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and the University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer is an archaeologist who held positions at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003).

Marion Rastelli works in Indology and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gerhard Oberhammer and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna (attested 2020).

Mark A. Nathan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert Buswell, and held posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo in 2010.

Mark Allon works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Australian National University, St John's College, and Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman, later holding posts at SOAS (~1995–2000) and the University of Sydney (~2002).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held appointments at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (~2005).

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford (~1984–1987) and University of Exeter (1987–1990). He held posts at the Workers' Educational Association, University of Plymouth (1990–1995), and Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).
Mark Elliott is a historian of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts at Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

Mark I. Wallace studied at UCSB, Princeton Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur. He taught at Merrimack College, Princeton Theological Seminary, Georgia State University (~1987–1989), and Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden was an Iranian and Central Asian linguist. He studied at Amsterdam and Utrecht under Jan Gonda, and later under Harold Walter Bailey and Walter Bruno Henning, before teaching at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).
